candidate_status: isolated, unpromoted; explicit HERot Polynomial factory injection only

secure_component.meaning: Exact six-field control tables and exact ciphertext/metadata parity vs ordinary facade with cache clears; secure timing is not a controlled speed comparison.

production_shape_public_tables.meaning: Public tables only on CPU; baseline warm per-modulus twiddle cache and fresh assembled contexts after JAX clears.

limitations: No live runtime edits, full transformer graph, TPU result or promotion.
Provider holds weak owner/master/context references and bounded metadata entries, without secret or key references.
Existing public NTT tables must remain immutable. Identity guards detect array replacement and metadata mutation, not in-place NumPy BAT content mutation.
Contiguous NumPy views can retain entire master backing buffers while a derived context is held, even after master wrapper collection; wrapper collection does not prove buffer release.
Logical host/JAX byte counts exclude existing twiddle caches, controls, ciphertexts, keys, compiler workspaces and allocator overhead. CPU JAX arrays are host RAM; no total-HBM claim.
The initial unit.log records3 failed guard tests because the first prototype rejected NumPy BAT fields; unit_v2.log and both numerical proofs use the corrected archived source.
Unsupported requests delegate to existing ordinary construction; its own global cache behavior is not changed or audited by this candidate.
